title: First Nations voices on water
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:50Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-04T09:46:58Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank point Managing water covers general water storage, trading and competing uses and mentions Aboriginal communities only as one user group, so it does not teach the First Nations focus on cultural flows and water ownership that this point needs.

draft.title: First Nations voices on water
card: Many First Nations peoples have lived in the Murray-Darling Basin for tens of thousands of years. Rivers, wetlands and floodplains are part of their Country, and carry culture, stories and responsibilities.
water that First Nations peoples own and manage, to care for Country and support their communities. The water can serve cultural, social, spiritual and economic needs.
water set aside to keep rivers healthy. These are managed for the environment, so they are not the same as cultural flows, which First Nations peoples own and manage.
First Nations peoples have said that their voices have often been left out of decisions about basin water. They ask to have a real say in how water is shared and managed.
draft.remember: Cultural flows are water owned and managed by First Nations peoples for Country and community.

a.q: Which statement best describes cultural flows?
opts: Water that First Nations peoples own and manage for Country
Water set aside by governments to keep rivers healthy
Water that farmers sell to towns during a drought
Water released from dams to reduce the risk of floods
a.why: Cultural flows are water that First Nations peoples own and manage to care for Country and support their communities. Water set aside to keep rivers healthy describes environmental flows, which are managed for the environment and not owned by First Nations peoples.
a.clue: Look for who owns and manages the water.

b.q: A First Nations group on the Darling River says it needs cultural flows, not just more environmental flows. Which reason best fits their view?
opts: They want water they own and manage to care for Country
They want governments to manage the water on their behalf
They want water set aside only for irrigated farms nearby
They want the river kept healthy without any role for them
b.why: Cultural flows give First Nations peoples ownership and management of water, so they can care for Country and support their communities. Environmental flows can help the river, but they are managed for the environment, so they do not give the group that control.
b.clue: Think about who makes the decisions about the water.

a.best: Water that First Nations peoples own and manage for Country

b.best: They want water they own and manage to care for Country

problems.detail: The card defines environmental flows ('water set aside to keep rivers healthy'), a term that belongs to point 3 (The Murray-Darling Basin Plan). Here it should only be mentioned as a contrast, not defined.

check.summary: The facts and both questions are sound, with one clear right answer each. The card defines environmental flows, which belongs to the Basin Plan point; it should only mention the term as a contrast.
